content: 1. The report UN GA A/67/373 is a note by the Secretary-General transmitting the report of the Director-General of the World Health Organization. It discusses options for strengthening and facilitating multisectoral action for the prevention and control of non-communicable diseases through effective partnerships. This document was accessed on October 1, 2016. 2. Barker G. conducted a review titled Adolescents, social support, and help-seeking behavior: an international literature review and programme consultation with recommendations for action. This document was accessed on October 1, 2016. 3. Devi BC, Tang TS, and Corbex M. conducted a pilot study in Sarawak, Malaysia, which demonstrated a reduction by half in the percentage of late-stage presentations for breast and cervical cancer over four years. The study focused on clinical downstaging and was published in the journal Annals of Oncology in 2007 (Volume 18, Issue 7, Pages 1172–1176). 4. The Guide to Cancer Early Diagnosis provides essential tools and strategies for improving early cancer detection and diagnosis. 5. The WHO PEN (Package of Essential Noncommunicable Disease Interventions) is an implementation tool designed for primary healthcare in low-resource settings. This document was accessed on October 1, 2016. 6. The Cancer Control: Diagnosis and Treatment guide by WHO outlines effective programmatic approaches for cancer diagnosis and treatment. This document was accessed on October 1, 2016. 7. The Medical Records Manual: A Guide for Developing Countries provides guidance on managing medical records in resource-limited settings. This document was accessed on October 1, 2016. 8. The guide Planning and Implementing Palliative Care Services: A Guide for Programme Managers offers strategies for establishing and managing palliative care services. This document was accessed on January 15, 2017. 9. Gabitova G. and Burke NJ. evaluated a mixed-methods approach to improving healthcare empowerment through breast cancer patient navigation in a safety-net setting. Their findings were published in BMC Health Services Research in 2014 (Volume 14, Article 407). 10. Ginsburg OM, Chowdhury M, Wu W, Chowdhury MT, Pal BC, Hasan R, et al. developed an mHealth model to increase clinic attendance for breast symptoms in rural Bangladesh. Their study explored whether bridging the digital divide could help close the cancer care gap. The findings were published in The Oncologist in 2014 (Volume 19, Issue 2, Pages 177–185). 11. Wadler BM, Judge CM, Prout M, Allen JD, and Geller AC. conducted a critical review on improving breast cancer control through the use of community health workers in South Africa. This review was published in the Journal of Oncology in 2011. 12. The technical brief Designing Health Financing Systems to Reduce Catastrophic Health Expenditure provides policy recommendations for minimizing financial burdens on patients. This document was accessed on October 1, 2016. 13. Balogh EP, Ganz PA, Murphy SB, Nass SJ, Ferrell BR, and Stovall E. summarized an Institute of Medicine workshop on patient-centered cancer treatment planning. The focus was on improving the quality of oncology care. The summary was published in The Oncologist in 2011 (Volume 16, Issue 12, Pages 1800–1805). 14. Young JL. authored The Hospital-Based Cancer Registry, which is included in the publication Cancer Registration: Principles and Methods. This document was accessed on January 15, 2017. 15. Bray F, Znaor A, Cueva P, Korir A, Swaminathan R, Ullrich A, et al. provided guidance on planning and developing population-based cancer registries in lowand middle-income settings. This publication was produced by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) and accessed on October 1, 2016.
